passage:
The government should absolutely pursue providing all citizens a universal basic income (UBI) funded by higher taxes on the wealthy. This policy addresses the growing inequality in our society, where the wealth gap continues to widen, leaving many struggling to meet basic needs. A UBI ensures that everyone has a financial safety net, promoting economic stability and dignity for all individuals, regardless of their circumstances.

Funding this initiative through higher taxes on the wealthy is not only fair but also a necessary step toward a more equitable society. The affluent have historically benefited from systemic advantages, and asking them to contribute more is a reasonable expectation. By redistributing wealth in this way, we can empower individuals to pursue education, entrepreneurship, or caregiving roles without the constant pressure of financial insecurity.

Moreover, UBI can stimulate the economy by increasing consumer spending, as individuals will have more disposable income. This will likely lead to job creation and innovation, offsetting any economic concerns surrounding the implementation of UBI. Ultimately, a universal basic income is a progressive and compassionate approach to ensuring that every citizen has the opportunity to thrive, fostering a healthier, more resilient society.
